properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 2:50AM MST until October 24 at 3:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Woodruff to Leupp.

* WHEN...Until 300 AM MST /400 AM MDT/ Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is imminent or
occurring. Further rises in the water levels are expected. Deadly
flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 243 AM MST /343 AM MDT/, river gauges along the Little
Colorado River at Woodruff, Holbrook, and Winslow reported
significant rises and elevated flow. Stages at both Holbrook and
Winslow are expected to reach action stage later this morning.
- For the Little Colorado River near Woodruff:
At 2:30am MST /3:30am MDT/ the stage was 14.72 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 15.28 feet is expected at 3:00am MST /4:00am
MDT/ Friday.
Impacts:
At 20.5 feet: Bankfull. Portions of residential yards flooded.

- For the Little Colorado River at Holbrook:
At 2:30am MST /3:30am MDT/ the stage was 14.22 feet.
Flood Stage is 15.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 16.41 feet is expected at 1:00pm MST /2:00pm
MDT/ Friday.
Impacts:
At 15.5 feet: Railroad bridge affected. Overflow on South Bank.

- For Little Colorado at Joseph City:
At 2:30am MST /3:30am MDT/ the stage was 5.93 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 6.5 feet is expected at 2:00pm MST /3:00pm
MDT/ Friday.
Impacts:
At 7.5 feet: Potential downstream lowland overflow.

- For the Little Colorado River at Winslow:
At 2:00am MST /3:00am MDT/ the stage was 17.04 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 17.23 feet is expected at 10:00am MST
/11:00am MDT/ Saturday.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow. Minor lowland overflow on right bank at Winslow.
At 18.0 feet: Flow above this level for approximately 6 hours or
more may cause erosion to the levee and eventual leakage or
failure.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Leupp, Birdsprings, Homolovi Ruins State Park, and Clear Creek
Reservoir.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.

surf. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding
possible.

* WHERE...Coastal Saint Lucie and Coastal Martin Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Saturday night.
For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Saturday night through
late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Some roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Shoreline erosion may occur. Rip currents
can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper
water.
properties.instruction:
Conditions favorable for coastal flooding are expected to
develop. Coastal residents should be alert for later statements
or warnings and take necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 23 at 12:32PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Invest 97W continues to develop over the northern Marshall Islands,
centered near 11N166E in the vicinity of Bikini and Rongelap Atolls.
97W is now the subject of a Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert (TCFA)
by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC), meaning it is expected
to develop into a significant tropical cyclone (a tropical
depression) within 24 hours. Himawari visible satellite imagery this
afternoon shows numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms across
the northern Marshall Islands, focused mainly over the
northwesternmost islands and atolls. Scatterometry data from this
morning shows fresh to strong west winds near Ujae and Ebadon Atolls,
and surface observations on Kwajalein Island are showing fresh west
winds with frequent strong gusts. Near-gale force gusts have been
observed with passing showers, and significant boat damage was
recently reported along west-facing exposures of Kwajalein as well.

Surging west winds are expected to continue across the western and
central Marshall Islands, south of Invest 97W's center, and boats
should be safely moved from west-facing exposures and secured, if
possible. Fresh to strong west winds will begin to shift
southwesterly tonight as 97W strengthens, and persist through Sunday
as 97W begins to lift north out of the RMI. Locally heavy showers
will be possible across the northern half of the Marshall Islands
through the weekend. Showers and winds will begin to diminish Sunday
night as 97W pulls farther away, but elevated west to southwest swell
associated with the disturbance may persist into early next week.
Elevated surf along west and south reefs may become hazardous this
weekend into early next week as these swells persist. This situation
will be closely monitored for additional impacts to the Marshall
Islands.

For more information on Invest 97W, see bulletins issued by JTWC
under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW.

properties.areaDesc: Archuleta, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 5:44PM MDT until October 23 at 5:45AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Archuleta County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 545 AM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring. Several structures are
flooded, and numerous roads remain closed due to flooding impacts
County wide. Streams will likely continue to rise due to excess
runoff and additional rainfall expected overnight.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 528 PM MDT, Public and local law enforcement reported numerous
impacts of flooding occurring across Archuleta County. Between
1.5 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 2 inches are possible in
the warned area this evening and overnight.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Pagosa Springs, Lonetree, Chimney Rock, Juanita, Gato, Pagosa
Junction, Chromo and Arboles.
- The San Juan River continues to rise, and is expected to exceed
Major Flood Stage late this evening and overnight. This flood
warning extends to tributaries, streams, creeks and low-land
areas beyond the San Juan River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING IN EFFECT UNTIL 545 AM MDT FRIDAY

trimmers, and outboard engines. It is also advised to limit outdoor
burning.
